GIVEN a PR commit WHEN CI runs THEN web-quality, dotnet-quality and PostgreSQL/pgvector integration checks execute and a mandatory failure prevents the source-quality gate.
GIVEN a tenant-isolation/RLS regression WHEN the PostgreSQL integration suite executes THEN CI fails.
GIVEN a clean PostgreSQL+pgvector database WHEN migrations run THEN the current schema is created successfully and the API can start against it.
GIVEN a green source-quality gate WHEN application images are built THEN exactly web/API/Worker release-candidate images are produced from the same commit.
GIVEN the built images WHEN downstream integration/E2E/security jobs execute THEN they load and test the exact image artifacts rather than rebuilding source.
GIVEN `compose.release.yml` WHEN inspected THEN web/API/Worker use `image:` references and contain no app `build:` directives.
GIVEN the exact containerized stack WHEN health smoke tests run THEN web serving, web->API proxying, API readiness and Worker processing/heartbeat succeed.
GIVEN an Owner Portal/internal authorization test WHEN a portal identity requests an internal protected resource THEN the request is denied without protected data leakage.
GIVEN an image with a vulnerability violating the configured blocking policy WHEN security scanning runs THEN `required-ci` fails and release/publish is blocked.
GIVEN a mandatory E2E or container-integration failure WHEN CI completes THEN `required-ci` fails.

GIVEN a successful `required-ci` WHEN the release bundle is generated THEN it contains the exact tested web/API/Worker images, Compose file, env example, checksums, build metadata, SBOMs and run instructions.
GIVEN the downloaded bundle on a clean Docker host WHEN images are loaded and documented environment values supplied THEN StrataAI2 starts without source, Node or .NET SDK.
GIVEN any released image WHEN its metadata is inspected THEN the originating repository, commit SHA/build ID and application version are identifiable.
GIVEN a pull request from an untrusted fork WHEN CI executes THEN privileged registry/project/production secrets are not exposed to the PR code.
GIVEN a successful trusted main/tag run WHEN images are published to GHCR THEN the published digests correspond to the same artifacts that passed `required-ci`, with no source rebuild.
GIVEN the release bundle WHEN SHA-256 verification runs THEN every listed artifact matches `SHA256SUMS`.
GIVEN a failed browser E2E test WHEN CI completes THEN diagnostic trace/screenshot evidence is retained according to artifact policy.
GIVEN a Worker job that is retried/replayed in integration testing WHEN processing completes THEN idempotency rules prevent duplicate material side effects.
GIVEN a SignalR/realtime feature is present WHEN its required CI test runs THEN an authorized client receives permitted events and an unauthorized/cross-tenant client does not.
GIVEN branch protection is configured WHEN a required underlying CI dependency fails/skips/cancels THEN the stable aggregate `required-ci` check cannot report success.
CI SHALL run for pull requests targeting the default branch and pushes to the default branch.
CI SHALL run for version/release tags used to create releasable builds.
CI SHOULD support manual `workflow_dispatch` for diagnostics/rebuild of the same source ref where permitted.
CI SHALL use workflow concurrency so superseded PR runs are cancelled, while main/tag release runs are not accidentally cancelled by unrelated commits.
Untrusted pull-request code SHALL NOT receive privileged production/project/registry secrets. Privileged release/publish operations SHALL be restricted to trusted repository refs/environments.
CI SHALL use the exact triggering commit SHA as the source identity. Release jobs SHALL NOT silently change refs or rebuild from a moving branch.
Third-party GitHub Actions used by the required pipeline SHOULD be pinned to immutable commit SHAs, with controlled dependency-update processes.
An initial metadata job SHALL calculate and expose commit SHA, short SHA, semantic/release version where available, workflow run ID and image tag/version metadata.
All later artifacts SHALL include source repository, commit SHA, workflow run ID and application version/build ID.
Web, API and Worker SHALL expose compatible build/revision metadata at runtime for diagnostics.
`web-quality` SHALL use the committed package lock and deterministic dependency installation such as `npm ci`.
`web-quality` SHALL run TypeScript type checking.
`web-quality` SHALL run ESLint with zero new warnings/errors under the configured policy.
`web-quality` SHALL run Vitest/React Testing Library tests.
Web tests SHALL include MUI component behaviour and accessibility-relevant interaction tests.
Kanban tests SHALL cover `dnd-kit` pointer and keyboard movement semantics where Kanban functionality is present.
`web-quality` SHALL produce a production Vite build.
Web test/coverage results SHALL be retained in a machine-readable format suitable for CI diagnosis.
`dotnet-quality` SHALL restore dependencies from committed project/lock configuration where applicable.
`dotnet-quality` SHALL compile Domain, Application, Infrastructure, API and Worker in Release configuration.
.NET warnings SHALL be treated as errors according to the repository policy.
`dotnet-quality` SHALL run xUnit unit/application tests across relevant projects.
API tests SHALL include authentication, authorization, validation and stable error-contract coverage.
Worker tests SHALL include job idempotency, retries, dead-letter/failure state and tenant-context propagation.
`postgres-integration` SHALL run against a real PostgreSQL 17+ instance with pgvector enabled rather than an in-memory/fake database.
CI SHALL apply all ordered schema migrations to an empty database and verify successful startup/schema compatibility.
CI SHALL test upgrade from at least the previous supported schema baseline to the current schema when such baseline exists.
CI SHALL verify required foreign keys, unique/check constraints and critical indexes where practicable.
CI SHALL verify PostgreSQL RLS/tenant isolation with at least two Organizations and attempted cross-tenant reads/writes.
CI SHALL verify that missing/malformed tenant context fails closed.
CI SHALL verify pgvector extension availability and representative semantic-vector persistence/query behaviour once vector functionality is implemented.
CI SHALL verify append-only/audit protections that are enforced at the database layer.
A `source-quality-gate` job SHALL depend on all required web, .NET and PostgreSQL source/integration jobs.
Container images SHALL NOT be considered releasable when any mandatory source-quality dependency fails.
The gate job SHALL contain explicit dependency-result validation rather than passing when an upstream required job is skipped unexpectedly.
After the source quality gate passes, CI SHALL build exactly three application images: `strataai-web`, `strataai-api`, and `strataai-worker`.
Each image SHALL be built exactly once per CI release candidate. Downstream test, scan, bundle and publish jobs SHALL consume those exact built image artifacts/digests.
CI SHALL NOT rebuild source separately for publishing or release bundling.
Images SHALL be tagged with immutable commit-derived tags such as `strataai-api:<sha>`, `strataai-worker:<sha>`, and `strataai-web:<sha>`.
Images SHALL include OCI labels for repository URL, revision/commit SHA, build/version and build timestamp.
Images SHALL be exported from the build job in a Docker-loadable/OCI-compatible artifact format that downstream jobs can load without rebuilding.
Build-time credentials/secrets SHALL use secure build-secret mechanisms and SHALL NOT remain in image layers/history.
The image build SHOULD use deterministic BuildKit/buildx caching keyed by dependency/lock inputs without allowing untrusted cache content to alter the final verified artifact.
`container-integration` SHALL download/load the exact web/API/Worker image artifacts created by `build-images-once`.
Integration CI SHALL boot a Compose/runtime topology containing the exact app images plus PostgreSQL+pgvector and object-storage parity where applicable (e.g. MinIO for local CI).
The integration Compose definition SHALL use `image:` for app services and SHALL NOT use `build:`.
CI SHALL validate database migration/startup using the containerized API/approved migration mechanism.
CI SHALL verify API liveness/readiness.
CI SHALL verify Worker liveness/operational readiness or an equivalent worker heartbeat/job-processing diagnostic.
CI SHALL verify the web container serves the compiled SPA.
CI SHALL verify web -> Nginx -> API reverse proxy health using the externally exposed web endpoint.
CI SHALL verify graceful container shutdown/restart behaviour for API and Worker at least in smoke/integration coverage.
Integration failures SHALL retain relevant container logs as CI artifacts.
`e2e` SHALL run against the exact containerized release candidate rather than separately launched development servers.
Browser E2E SHALL use Playwright or an approved equivalent.
E2E SHALL cover at minimum authenticated internal-app startup, core navigation and one representative create/read/update flow once those features exist.
When implemented, E2E SHALL cover owner-portal isolation from internal Council/Management data.
When implemented, E2E SHALL cover representative Kanban drag/drop persistence.
When implemented, E2E/integration SHALL cover SignalR/realtime update/reconnect behaviour.
When implemented, E2E/integration SHALL cover a representative Worker/outbox job progressing from persisted request through completed domain state.
Failed Playwright runs SHALL retain traces/screenshots/videos according to the configured failure-artifact policy.
CI SHALL run dependency vulnerability checks appropriate to Node and .NET.
CI SHALL run secret-detection scanning against repository content/history according to the configured policy.
CI SHALL scan all three exact application images for known vulnerabilities before release/publish.

The blocking vulnerability policy SHALL be documented. Initial default SHOULD block newly introduced exploitable Critical vulnerabilities and SHOULD block High vulnerabilities when a fix is available, subject to an explicit audited exception process.
CI SHALL generate an SBOM for web, API and Worker images in a standard machine-readable format such as SPDX or CycloneDX.
CI SHOULD generate GitHub artifact attestations/SLSA-compatible provenance for release artifacts/images where repository/platform capability permits.
Security scan output SHALL be retained for diagnosis and release evidence.
A failed mandatory security gate SHALL prevent successful release/publish.
A stable final aggregate job/check named `required-ci` (or another deliberately stable name) SHALL depend on all mandatory source-quality, image-build, container-integration, E2E and security jobs.
Branch/ruleset protection SHOULD require the stable final aggregate check rather than depending directly on every internal job name.
`required-ci` SHALL fail if a mandatory dependency failed, was cancelled, or was unexpectedly skipped.
Release/publish jobs SHALL depend on successful `required-ci`.
After `required-ci`, CI SHALL create `strataai2-docker-bundle-<sha>`.
The bundle SHALL contain the exact tested web/API/Worker image archives.
The bundle SHALL contain `compose.release.yml` that references the included image tags and has no app `build:` directives.
The bundle SHALL contain `.env.release.example` containing placeholders/documented configuration only, never real secrets.
The bundle SHALL contain `SHA256SUMS`.
The bundle SHALL contain build metadata including repository, commit SHA, workflow run, image tags/digests and build version.
The bundle SHALL contain SBOMs for web/API/Worker and security/provenance metadata required by policy.
The bundle SHALL contain concise run instructions covering image load, environment setup, `docker compose up`, health verification and shutdown.
The release bundle SHALL be usable on a clean Docker Desktop/Engine machine without Node, .NET SDK or source checkout.
CI SHALL verify checksums and bundle completeness before uploading the artifact.
PR artifacts SHOULD have a shorter retention period (default target: 14 days); main/tag release artifacts SHOULD have a longer retention period (default target: 90 days or repository policy).
On trusted default-branch and/or version-tag runs, CI MAY publish the exact already-tested images to GHCR.
Registry publication SHALL use the exact artifact/digest that passed `required-ci`, not a source rebuild.
Mutable convenience tags such as `latest` MAY exist, but deployments/releases SHALL be traceable to immutable SHA tags/digests.
PRs from untrusted forks SHALL not receive package-write credentials.
Registry/package permissions SHALL use least privilege.
CI SHALL upload machine-readable test result summaries where practical.
Test names, metadata or traceability manifests SHALL reference PRD/ARCH acceptance/test IDs for implementation-ticket traceability.
Pull requests SHOULD include or link to the successful CI run and relevant executed test evidence before associated PRD tickets are closed.
Build/release metadata SHALL make it possible to determine which PRD implementation commit produced any running image.
CI SHALL run for pull requests targeting the default branch and pushes to the default branch.

Each Organization MAY configure one primary shared mailbox with provider, address, connection/sync state, inbound/outbound flags, default signature and intake Board/List.

Users SHALL explicitly select attachments; relationship to a Document never automatically authorizes sending it.
HTML/content SHALL be sanitized and hostile email/prompt injection SHALL never override system instructions.

Portal SHALL be a separate authorization surface; PortalAccess SHALL never imply OrganizationMember, BoardMember or internal Card access.
Any current Council Member or assigned Strata Manager MAY invite an owner/resident subject to Organization policy; invitation authority SHALL not broaden the inviter's own internal permissions.
Portal invitations SHALL use secure single-use expiring revocable tokens bound to Organization and invited email and SHALL reuse existing User identity when present.
PortalAccess lifecycle SHALL support INVITED, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, REVOKED and EXPIRED and MAY link one or more authorized StrataLot relationships.
Portal home SHALL expose Organization/property info, associated Units, published Documents, configured contacts, issue submission/status and notifications only.
PortalFolder SHALL support parent/child hierarchy, name/description/rank/visibility/lifecycle and authorized Council/Manager management.

PortalDocumentPublication SHALL explicitly publish an existing Document into a PortalFolder with display title, publication/effective/expiry dates, visibility scope and DRAFT/PUBLISHED/UNPUBLISHED/ARCHIVED state.
Internal Document relationships SHALL never imply portal publication; unpublished/draft/confidential Documents SHALL remain hidden.
Publication visibility SHALL support ALL_PORTAL_USERS, SPECIFIC_UNITS, SPECIFIC_USERS, OWNERS_ONLY, RESIDENTS_ONLY and extensible groups.
Portal users SHALL browse/open/download permitted Documents but SHALL not edit authoritative Documents or see internal comments/relationships.
Portal search SHALL index only portal-visible folders/Documents and SHALL never leak internal titles, counts, snippets or hidden records.
Issue intake SHALL map internal workflow to simplified portal statuses RECEIVED, UNDER_REVIEW, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_FOR_INFORMATION, RESOLVED and CLOSED.
Portal notifications SHALL cover invitations, document publications/updates, issue acknowledgement/status and intended correspondence without confidential previews.
All portal APIs/downloads/signed URLs SHALL enforce portal-specific server-side authorization independently of internal Board authorization.

Portal security testing SHALL include horizontal owner access, cross-Organization access, unit restrictions, expired/revoked invitation/access, direct URL/signed URL abuse, folder enumeration and search leakage.
